newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold ends shade down, little physical demand.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends shade down, little physical demand.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended a hint lower on Tuesday compared to its previous New York close after a day of caution in Asia, with little movement in gold prices and only marginal physical demand, bullion dealers said.
"I am a little bit cautious," said a senior dealer at a local bullion firm.
Traders said the market had seen some selling, but the afternoon had remained quiet with little interest from European markets and a bearish mantle still hovered over gold.
Bullion ended at US$347.40/90 an ounce against New York's US$347.50/348.00 close on Monday.
The main issue was the drop in open interest on COMEX, dealers said.
"Basically everybody has finished shortcovering and if you can't buy higher, you sell lower," said another bullion chief.
Dealers said that if open interest fell further, it would indicate long liquidation and a loss in downward momentum for gold prices.
"If open interest increases, it's not so good because people would be building up fresh short positions," one source said.

Data released Monday showed that COMEX gold open interest fell a further 2,862 lots Friday to 166,622 contracts, the lowest level since September last year, after funds covered short positions, traders in New York said.
The sharp drop in gold prices overnight had failed to spur physical demand in Asia as buyers were looking for further price drops, bullion traders said.
Dealers saw the market dropping further in coming days
Local gold ended HK$40 lower at HK$3,221 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange dropped to -4.00 from its previous fix -3.00
